title: Implement Keyboard Shortcut for Toggling Timestamps
description: ChatterDock is a simple C-based desktop application that provides a basic chat-like interface. Users have requested a new quality-of-life feature: the ability to show or hide timestamps next to messages using a keyboard shortcut. This task requires implementing this feature over two separate development sessions, simulating a developer starting a task, pausing, and then resuming work later. The agent must first set up the event infrastructure for the shortcut and then, in a second session, implement the logic that uses this event to change the UI.

project_spec.name: ChatterDock
project_spec.description:
ChatterDock is a lightweight desktop hub that lets users aggregate and interact with multiple social feeds (e-mail, micro-blogs, group chats) from a single, multi-window workspace. The application showcases an event-driven backbone where every inbound message, user action, or plugin signal is converted into an event object that propagates through a non-blocking dispatcher. Features such as user-selectable themes, configurable keyboard shortcuts, and per-window layouts are persisted as user_preferences and re-emitted at runtime so the UI refreshes instantly when settings change.

A built-in plugin_system encourages community extensions—e.g., a “Birthday Notifier” or a “Trending-Hashtag Lens”—by exposing a small C API that registers new commands and subscribes to the global event bus (leveraging the Observer_Pattern). Because each plugin speaks the same Command_Pattern contract, users can bind keyboard shortcuts to trigger plugin commands or core actions alike, giving ChatterDock a social-first yet highly hackable personality.
dependencies: GTK 4.x – native widgets, multi_window support, built-in event loop
GLib/GObject – signal (Observer) framework and main loop integration
libpeas – plugin_system loader for C plugins at runtime
Cairo/Pango – themable rendering of text and graphics
